title: CODA: A Computation-Data Decoupled Dataflow Paradigm for DNN Computing on NPUs
evidence_span: CODA models computation and per-tensor storage/movement independently using a non-uniform loop space, expanding NPU mapping options beyond coupled dataflows; the official description presents improved mapping expressiveness without numeric results.
problem: Coupled computation-data dataflows force tensors to share storage structures and paths, limiting mappings as NPU memory hierarchies become complex.
method_or_artifact: Computation-data decoupled dataflow representation with tensor-wise mapping and non-uniform loop-space modeling.
workload_or_benchmark: DNN operators mapped to NPUs; workloads, hardware hierarchy, search method, and performance baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: NPU with hierarchical on-chip memory and configurable tensor movement; buffer sizes, bandwidth, and execution model are unspecified.
limits: The description omits latency, energy, area, search cost, and benchmark coverage.
A larger mapping space may increase compiler/search complexity.
Official description only; accelerator claims require paper-level evaluation.

title: G-Power: Architecture-Level GPU Power Modeling with Aggregated Knowledge Foundations from Known GPUs
evidence_span: G-Power addresses sparse and low-quality microbenchmark power labels by aggregating knowledge from known GPUs into an architecture-level model; the official description claims improved power-model accuracy beyond AccelWattch without numeric values.
problem: GPU power models trained mostly on simple microbenchmarks lack accuracy for complex architectures because collecting power labels is expensive.
method_or_artifact: Knowledge-aggregated architecture-level GPU power model intended to transfer across known GPU designs.
workload_or_benchmark: GPU architecture and power workloads; GPU generations, labels, features, transfer protocol, and baseline accuracy are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Modern GPU architecture-level power estimation; counters, microarchitecture parameters, and measurement boundary are unspecified.
baselines: AccelWattch and existing architecture-level GPU power models
limits: The description omits error metrics, GPU holdouts, label cost, workload diversity, and transfer conditions.
Knowledge aggregation may leak architecture-specific information or fail on unseen designs.
Official description only; power-model claims require cross-GPU validation.

title: Compilation Tells Energy: Rethinking Power Modeling for DNN Accelerator Agile Design
evidence_span: The methodology extracts compiler intermediate-representation features from RTL-generator toolchains and uses multi-task learning to predict accelerator power before synthesis, exploiting workload-hardware coupling; the official description claims practical push-button accuracy without numeric results.
problem: Early RTL-generator workflows lack fast power feedback, while simulator-based modeling is too laborious and generic ML misses software-hardware coupling.
method_or_artifact: Compiler-IR feature extraction and multi-task learning for early DNN accelerator energy prediction.
workload_or_benchmark: DNN accelerator RTL-generator designs and compiler IRs; power labels, synthesis baselines, accuracy, and design space are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: RTL-generated DNN accelerators with compiler and synthesis flow; technology, clock, voltage, and power boundary are unspecified.
metrics: Practical push-button power prediction claimed qualitatively
limits: The description omits prediction error, label cost, synthesis correlation, model scope, and hardware details.
Compiler features may be toolchain-specific and fail under new generators or workloads.
Official description only; power claims require calibrated silicon/synthesis validation.

title: Ecprefix: Erasure-Coded Prefix KV Cache for Optimizing Load Balancing in Large Language Model Serving
evidence_span: ECPrefix replaces replicated hot prefix KV caches with erasure-coded profile-guided objects distributed across nodes, using adaptive striping and pipelined reads; evaluation reports up to 52.3% lower time-to-first-token than existing systems.
problem: Prefix-cache replication leaves a few nodes overloaded despite added storage, limiting load balance in distributed LLM serving.
method_or_artifact: Erasure-coded prefix KV-cache distribution with adaptive striping and pipelined retrieval.
workload_or_benchmark: Large-language-model serving with hot prefix caches; models, node count, workload distribution, coding parameters, and baseline systems are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Distributed serving nodes with storage/networked KV caches; bandwidth, failure model, memory, and compute architecture are unspecified.
limits: The description omits throughput, tail latency, coding/storage overhead, failure recovery, and workload variance.
Erasure coding trades replication cost for encoding/decoding and read amplification.
Official description only; serving claims require trace and cluster verification.

title: Factored Floating-Point MAC: Eliminating Redundant Normalization for Energy-Efficient Systolic Arrays
evidence_span: Factored-FPMAC uses 4:2 carry-save adders and redundant representation inside systolic arrays, deferring normalization to unified post-processing to remove repeated rounding and wide carry-propagate adders; numerical outcomes are not included in the official description.
problem: Conventional floating-point FMA in long GEMM chains repeats normalization and rounding, causing numerical error, delay, and energy overhead.
method_or_artifact: Factored floating-point MAC with carry-save accumulation and deferred unified normalization.
workload_or_benchmark: Floating-point systolic-array GEMM and related scientific/ML workloads; precision, numerical error, area, power, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Systolic array using 4:2 CSAs and floating-point redundant representation; process, frequency, pipeline, and normalization hardware are unspecified.
metrics: Redundant normalization and CPA removal claimed qualitatively
Numerical and energy benefits claimed qualitatively
limits: The description omits precision/error, PPA, timing, area, and workload results.
Deferred normalization may affect overflow, rounding, and numerical reproducibility.
Official description only; arithmetic claims require bit-accurate and hardware verification.

title: A Hamiltonian-Guided Pre-Trainer for Variational Quantum Algorithms
evidence_span: HGP constructs VQA initial parameters by iteratively optimizing Hamiltonian-guided low-dimensional parameter blocks, reconstructing analytic landscapes from a few quantum measurements instead of static guesses; the description claims improved initialization against local minima without numeric results.
problem: Variational quantum algorithms are sensitive to poor initialization and can trap optimizers in suboptimal local minima.
method_or_artifact: Hamiltonian-guided parameter blocking and low-dimensional global pre-training from limited quantum measurements.
workload_or_benchmark: Variational quantum algorithm optimization; Hamiltonians, qubit counts, noise, measurement budgets, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Quantum processor or simulator providing measurements and Hamiltonian structure; device noise, circuit depth, and optimizer are unspecified.
metrics: Improved initialization and local-minimum avoidance claimed qualitatively
limits: The description omits convergence, measurement overhead, quantum-resource cost, noise robustness, and benchmark results.
Low-dimensional landscape reconstruction may fail for highly entangled or nonlocal Hamiltonians.
Official description only; quantum optimization claims require reproducible simulations or hardware runs.

title: Efficient HLS Accelerator Floorplan on Multi-Die FPGA Aided by Graph Neural Networks
evidence_span: The framework predicts slot-level floorplan quality and congestion for HLS designs on multi-die FPGAs using a GNN, reducing iterative Vitis implementations; the predictor reports 84.13% accuracy and 0.86 F1 for congestion prediction, with an average inference-time reduction claim not numerically exposed in the description.
problem: Cross-die boundary delays and local congestion make multi-die FPGA HLS floorplanning expensive to tune through repeated implementation runs.
method_or_artifact: Graph neural network floorplan-quality and congestion predictor for slot-level multi-die FPGA placement.
workload_or_benchmark: HLS accelerator floorplans on multi-die FPGAs and Vitis implementation iterations; designs, slot topology, timing, and baseline runtime are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Multi-die FPGA with cross-die delays and congestion; device family, Vitis version, clock targets, and implementation flow are unspecified.
limits: The description omits prediction calibration, PPA/timing outcomes, inference speed, design diversity, and false-positive cost.
Predictor quality may be device- and tool-version-specific.
Official description only; FPGA floorplanning claims require implementation reproducibility.

title: Weaver: Stratified Expert Scheduling for Memory-Constrained MoE Inference
evidence_span: Weaver schedules low-score experts on CPU during GPU attention using prior-layer inputs, retains high-score experts for accuracy, and uses stratified prefetching to overlap offload with computation; the official description claims improved memory-constrained MoE inference without numeric results.
problem: MoE parameters exceed device capacity, while CPU offloading leaves CPU cycles idle during GPU attention and increases latency.
method_or_artifact: Score-stratified expert scheduling, approximate low-importance experts, and predictive prefetch overlap.
workload_or_benchmark: Memory-constrained MoE inference; model suite, CPU/GPU hardware, approximation error, latency, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Heterogeneous CPU-GPU inference with expert offloading and limited device memory; interconnect, bandwidth, and scheduling runtime are unspecified.
limits: The description omits throughput, tail latency, accuracy, CPU utilization, bandwidth, and model details.
Approximating low-score experts may fail under distribution shift or adversarial routing.
Official description only; serving claims require workload and quality verification.
